title: Bibimbap
subtitle: Korean mixed rice bowl with vegetables and egg
excerpt: Korea's most famous rice bowl: a bed of warm rice topped with individually seasoned vegetables, minced beef, a fried egg, and a generous spoonful of gochujang, mixed together vigorously at the table. Every component simple; together they are extraordinary.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bibimbap (literally 'mixed rice') is one of Korea's most recognisable and beloved dishes, served in homes, restaurants, and street food stalls across the country. Its origins are debated; one tradition holds that it developed from the custom of mixing together leftover banchan (side dishes) with rice at the end of a meal. Another theory links it to ritual ancestral foods. The key feature of bibimbap is that each topping is prepared and seasoned separately before being arranged on the rice, so that each individual component has its own distinct flavour and colour. The dolsot version (served in a sizzling stone pot) creates a crust on the bottom of the rice. Gochujang (Korean fermented chilli paste) is the essential condiment, added at the table.

content.text: Prepare each vegetable topping separately, seasoned individually, so they each have a distinct flavour. The beef is seasoned with soy sauce and sesame oil. The egg yolk should be runny so it enriches the sauce when mixed. Gochujang is essential and cannot be substituted; it is available in most supermarkets.
Season the beef with half the soy sauce, garlic, and a dash of sesame oil. Cook in a hot pan until browned. Saute each vegetable briefly with a pinch of salt, keeping them separate.
Dress the blanched spinach with the remaining soy sauce and sesame oil. Season each component to taste.

Divide the warm rice between two large bowls. Arrange the beef and each vegetable in separate sections over the rice. Place a fried egg in the centre of each bowl. Add a tablespoon of gochujang. Scatter sesame seeds. To eat: mix everything vigorously together with a spoon.
